verdict: Memory erupts (WDC +16%, MU +8.7% to ATH) on US-Iran peace deal; MU Q3 earnings June 24 is next binary; AVGO guide-miss digesting; FSLR Section 232 tariff due ~June 26; HIVE $220M GPU deal closed — bull tone.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (Last 24-72h)

**Memory sector erupts on macro catalyst.** A US-Iran peace deal announced ~June 20 triggered a broad global market rally that amplified already-strong memory momentum: **WDC +16%** (33% over three sessions), **MU +8.7%** to new all-time records (~$1,134-$1,152), **MRVL +7.27%**, **AVGO +4.7%** (recovery from June 3 earnings sell-off). **Micron fiscal Q3 earnings are due June 24** — an imminent event risk; consensus expects another HBM/server DRAM beat.

**HIVE Digital $220M sovereign GPU deal (June 18).** BUZZ HPC (HIVE's AI subsidiary) announced a 3-year, $220M sovereign AI cloud contract: 2,304 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs; Bell Canada + Cohere + Hypertec as partners. Projected ~$70M ARR when fully deployed. Stock +7.8% on the day. B. Riley raised target to $8, Rosenblatt to $5.50.

**Section 232 solar tariff: clock running.** Presidential decision deadline ~June 26 (90-day window from March 28 Commerce report). Proposed structure: ~$0.20/W on modules + Tariff Rate Quota. FSLR is the prime domestic beneficiary. Solar stocks +40% YTD in anticipation; UBS raised FSLR to $330 (~June 11, stock +9%).

**AVGO sector tone reset still digesting.** June 3 Q2 print: AI chip revenue $10.8B (+143% YoY) but Q3 guide of $16B missed $17.2B consensus — stock fell ~12%. FY26 $56B and FY27 $100B+ AI semi targets reaffirmed. Drag on MRVL, AMD, broader cohort post-print; now recovering.

## Signal Scan (1-6)

1. **DRAM/HBM pricing:** No fresh June spot/contract print this week. Last formal data: TrendForce Q2 forecast +58-63% QoQ conventional DRAM, +70-75% NAND. Pricing supercycle intact; HBM ASPs have seen modest compression as all three suppliers ramp HBM3E. Quiet.
2. **HBM4 ramp:** SK Hynix delayed HBM4 capacity from Q2 → Q3 2026 (HBM3E demand too strong to idle lines). Samsung targeting 250K wafers/month HBM by end-2026 (+47%). No new development last 72h — delay slightly pushes peak-competition window to late 2026/early 2027.
3. **Hyperscaler capex:** No new print last 72h. Last confirmed guidance: MSFT ~$190B, Alphabet ~$190B, Meta $125-145B, Amazon ~$200B — combined ~$725B, above baseline $600-700B. Zero guide-down signals.
4. **AMD MI400/Helios + Custom ASICs:** On track 2H-2026; no fresh news last 72h. AWS Trainium3 GA, Trainium4 (late 2026/early 2027) on roadmap. Broadcom + Marvell hold ~95% custom-ASIC co-design market.
5. **Optical/Photonics:** No fresh news last 72h. COHR 1.6T transceivers at OFC 2026 support three laser routes (SiPh / InP EML / GaAs VCSEL). InP supply gap ~70% persists.
6. **Solar:** Section 232 pending (~June 26 deadline). No final announcement yet.

No notable moves last 24-72h for: SNDK, STX, RMBS, MRAM, ALAB, COHR, LITE, CIEN, ENPH, NXT, ARRY, NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU.

## Context vs. Baseline

- DRAM supercycle tracking ahead of baseline: Q1 actual +93-98% QoQ vs. baseline ~90-95%; Q2 forecast +58-63% confirms continuation.
- Hyperscaler capex well above baseline: $725B combined vs. $600-700B baseline — structurally bullish for HBM, optical, power.
- SK Hynix HBM4 delay pushes peak-supply competition slightly to late 2026/early 2027 — narrows the near-term correction window from the baseline's key caveat.
- HIVE's $220M BUZZ HPC contract is the type of GPU/HPC win the watchlist specifically flags.

## Most Important Development

**Memory names surge to all-time highs (WDC +16%, MU +8.7%) on US-Iran peace deal macro lift, with Micron fiscal Q3 earnings 3 days out (June 24).** This is the supercycle thesis confirming in live price action. The June 24 print is the next binary — watch for HBM volume mix, ASP trajectory, and 2H pricing color vs. the baseline's key risk: SK Hynix's "correction after 2026" warning as capacity expansions complete.
